chunks: From Ibn Mahbub from Abdallah ibn Sinan who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Everything in which there is Haram and Halal, it is Halal for you forever until you know the Haram in it specifically so you abandon it.

key_terms.بِعَيْنِهِ: Specifically / by its own distinct identity

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on food or items where Halal and Haram are mixed but cannot be distinguished?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) articulates the foundational principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) regarding mixed items, asserting that the default state of permissibility remains until the specific Haram component is distinctly identified. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach of easing burdens on the believer by maintaining the status quo of Halal in cases of general doubt, requiring positive proof of impurity to alter the ruling. This principle is crucial in *fiqh al-mukhtalat* (jurisprudence of mixed items), ensuring that uncertainty does not automatically render an item Haram.

en.ammaar-muslim: 2. [2/93] al-Faqih and al-Tahdhib: From Ibn Mahbub from Abdallah b. Sinan who said:
Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: everything which has both Halal and Haram [elements mixed into it] then it is Halal for you forever until you know the Haram in it specifically so you abandon it.
